item.title: Weather Alert: AIT Taipei Typhoon Advisory
item.content:encoded:
Weather Alert: AIT Taipei Typhoon Advisory

Location: Northern and Eastern Taiwan with possible island-wide impacts

Event: Typhoon Champi is forecast to have possible impacts to Taiwan in the coming three days. The typhoon may bring significant risks from high winds and torrential rainfall. Residents and visitors should prepare for heavy rain, strong winds, dangerous storm surge, and possible flooding.

Actions to take:

  • Monitor local news for updates.

item.title: Message for U.S. Citizens: 2026 Urban Resilience (Air Defense) Exercises
item.content:encoded:
Message for U.S. Citizens: 2026 Urban Resilience (Air Defense) Exercises

Location: Taiwan

Event: Planned Transportation and Communications Disruption

Taiwan’s national and local authorities have announced the 2026 Urban Resilience (Air Defense) Exercises.  These drills will impact transportation and communications.  In addition to practicing alarm transmission, evacuation and sheltering, traffic control, and disaster rescue, this year the drills will include a first-ever nationwide simulation of mobile internet disruptions. The exercise tests national security resilience, public preparedness, and backup communications in the event of emergencies, natural disasters, or cyber-attacks.

This drill affects regions of Taiwan on separate dates:

item.title: Due to heavy rain and flooding, AIT Kaohsiung office will be closed on June 26, 2026
item.content:encoded:
Due to heavy rain and flooding, AIT Kaohsiung office will be closed on June 26, 2026

Due to heavy rain and flooding, the AIT office in Kaohsiung is closed on June 26, 2026.

The AIT main office in Taipei is currently operating as normal.

All U.S. citizens residing in or visiting these areas are urged to monitor local news for the latest safety and weather information. For medical or fire emergencies, please call 119.

For more information:

AIT Website: https://www.ait.org.tw/services/
Taiwan Central Weather Administration:  Home | Central Weather Administration

item.title: Voting in U.S. Elections from Overseas
item.content:encoded:
Voting in U.S. Elections from Overseas

Be an Active Voter by taking the necessary steps to vote in the 2026 U.S. elections. Voter registration deadlines vary by state. Some states require voters to be registered 30 days before an election. Check the Federal Voting Assistance Program website (www.FVAP.gov) to find more information on the deadline in your state. Whether you are a first-time voter or have voted absentee in previous elections, you should complete a Voter Registration and Absentee Ballot Request (FPCA) each year to ensure you are able to participate in elections as an overseas absentee voter.

You can drop off your FPCA at the American Institute in Taiwan to be returned to your local election officials free of charge, or you can mail it directly at your own expense.

If you have already completed a FPCA in 2026, check your state’s voter registration verification website, or contact your local election office, to check the status of your absentee ballot request. Using the FPCA ensures that your state will send your ballot to you at least 45 days before the election.
